objectives: Explain how Q,K,V come from the same sequence
Trace how every token attends to every other

slides.title: Part 1 — Why self-attention
slides.body: You derived general attention with separate inputs. Self-attention is the special case — Q, K, V all from one sequence — that actually powers every transformer. The specialization has profound consequences for *path length* and *cost*.

slides.title: Q, K, V from the same sequence
slides.body: In **self**-attention, one input sequence $X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ produces all three: $Q=XW^Q,;K=XW^K,;V=XW^V$. Every token simultaneously (a) asks a question (its query), (b) advertises what it offers (its key), and (c) carries content (its value) — *to and from every token in the same sequence, itself included*. One self-attention layer therefore rewrites each token as a relevance-weighted blend of the entire sequence: pure **contextualization**. The word *bank* beside *river* vs beside *money* leaves the layer with different output vectors solely because its attention row points at different neighbors — meaning is computed from context, and it emerged from training, not rules.

slides.title: The killer property: O(1) path length
slides.body: This is the deep reason transformers beat RNNs. In an RNN the information path from token 1 to token 500 has length 499 (gradient must survive 499 multiplicative steps → vanishing). In self-attention, **any two positions are connected in a single layer** — maximum path length is $\mathcal{O}(1)$, independent of distance. Gradient between distant tokens no longer has to thread hundreds of Jacobians. Constant path length is *why* transformers learn long-range dependencies (agreement, coreference, document structure) that recurrence could not. Hold this next to the cost fact below — together they define the entire research landscape.

slides.title: Every row is a distribution over the sequence
slides.body: The weight matrix $A=\text{softmax}(QK^{T}/\sqrt{d_k})$ is $n\times n$; row $i$ is a probability distribution over which tokens token $i$ reads from. A 'focused' head has a near one-hot row (attend to one antecedent); a 'diffuse' head spreads weight (average context). Reading these rows is how interpretability researchers reverse-engineer what a layer does — and what you should do to debug a model that attends to the wrong things.

slides.title: Same formula, shared source — and why that matters
slides.body: $\text{SelfAttn}(X)=\text{softmax}\!\big((XW^Q)(XW^K)^{T}/\sqrt{d_k}\big)(XW^V)$. Structurally identical to general attention; the *only* change is that Q, K, V are three learned **views of one sequence**. That sharing is what makes it (a) parallel across all positions and (b) $\mathcal{O}(1)$ path length. Reconstruct the specialization and its permutation-equivariance property (the reason positional encoding will be needed):

question.question: From attention to SELF-attention
question.goal: You already derived attention; specialize it to one sequence attending to itself.

steps.prompt: In self-attention, where do Q, K, V come from?
steps.motivation: All three are linear projections of the SAME input — every token queries the same set it belongs to.

options: All three are linear projections of the same input sequence
Q from input, K/V from separate memory

steps.reveal: Q=XWq, K=XWk, V=XWv from the same X — each token attends over the whole sequence (incl. itself).

steps.prompt: Why is self-attention permutation-equivariant, and what fixes it?
steps.motivation: It is a set operation with no built-in order; order must be injected explicitly.

rubricCriteria.description: it treats the input as a set — no inherent order
so order must be added explicitly to the embeddings

hints: Shuffle the tokens — does the math change?
steps.reveal: No positional term ⇒ permuting inputs permutes outputs identically; positional encodings break that symmetry.

question.finalResult: Self-attention = Attention(XWq, XWk, XWv) — one sequence attending to itself

slides.title: Part 3 — Worked example & the quadratic wall
Cost: O(n²) in sequence length — quantified
slides.body: $S=QK^{T}$ has $n^2$ entries; forming and softmaxing it is $\mathcal{O}(n^2 d_k)$ time and (naively) $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ memory **per head per layer**. At $n=4096$ that's ~16.7M scores per head; with 32 heads × 32 layers, the attention matrices alone are billions of numbers. This single quadratic is the defining engineering constraint of transformers and spawned an entire field of fixes: **FlashAttention** (IO-aware exact attention that never materializes the full $n\times n$ matrix — same math, tiled to fit SRAM), sliding-window/sparse attention (Longformer, BigBird), and linear-attention approximations (Performer). Knowing *which* of these preserves exact attention vs approximates it is a real engineering decision.

question.question: FlashAttention makes long-context attention much cheaper in memory. How?
options: It computes exact attention but never materializes the full n×n score matrix — it tiles the computation to stay in fast SRAM
It approximates softmax with a linear kernel
It drops attention to a local window
question.explanation: FlashAttention is exact — same result as standard attention. The win is systems-level: it fuses the softmax and matmul and tiles them so the giant n×n matrix never leaves fast on-chip memory, cutting memory traffic dramatically. It does not change the math, unlike sliding-window or linear-attention approximations.

slides.title: Part 4 — Causal masking: the pitfall that bites
Don't let a token see its own answer
slides.body: For autoregressive generation, token $i$ must predict token $i{+}1$ from tokens $\le i$ only. During teacher-forced training the whole sequence is present at once, so *without intervention* position $i$'s attention can read positions $>i$ — including the very token it's supposed to predict. The model then learns a trivial copy shortcut: low training loss, **garbage at inference** where the future doesn't exist. Fix: a **causal mask** — add $-\infty$ to all scores $S_{ij}$ with $j>i$ *before* softmax, so future weights become exactly 0 (a lower-triangular attention pattern). Encoders (BERT) intentionally omit this (bidirectional); decoders (GPT) require it. This train/inference mismatch is one of the most common and most silent transformer bugs.

question.question: In causal self-attention, can the token at position 3 attend to the token at position 7?
options: No — position 7 is in the future and is masked out
Yes — every token attends to every other token
Only if positions 4, 5, 6 are also attended to
question.explanation: Causal masking zeros attention from position i to any j > i. Position 3 may attend to 0,1,2,3 — never 4+. This is exactly what makes the model autoregressive: a prediction can only depend on the past.

question.question: Sort each transformer family by whether its self-attention uses a causal mask.

items.label: Encoder stack of a translation model

question.explanation: Autoregressive decoders (GPT, LLaMA) must not see the future, so they mask. Encoders (BERT, the encoder side of a seq2seq model) classify/encode a complete input, so every token may see every other — no mask.

slides.title: More boundary conditions
slides.body:
- **Padding mask:** batched variable-length sequences need pad positions masked too, independently of the causal mask.
- **Encoder vs decoder vs cross-attention:** self-attention (one sequence), masked self-attention (decoder), and cross-attention (decoder queries attend to encoder keys/values) are the same primitive with different Q/K/V sources and masks.
- **KV-cache:** at inference, past K/V are cached so each new token is $\mathcal{O}(n)$ not $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ — the cache's memory is what multi-head's GQA later optimizes.

question.question: Diagnose the train/inference gap.
question.scenario: An autoregressive LM produces fluent text under teacher forcing in training but garbage when generating at inference. Attention is suspected.

rubricCriteria.description: the causal mask is missing/incorrect, so positions attend to future tokens in training
the model learns to 'cheat' by peeking ahead — impossible at inference
fix: apply the causal (lower-triangular) attention mask

question.explanation: Without a causal mask, training lets each position see the answer (future tokens); at inference there is no future, so the learned shortcut collapses.

hints: Autoregressive = predict next token from past only.
What must a position NOT be allowed to see?
slides.workedSolution: It masks (−∞ before softmax) all positions j>i for query i, enforcing left-to-right information flow so training matches autoregressive inference.

question.question: What does the causal mask in self-attention do?
options: Zeros attention weights to future positions so a token cannot see what it must predict
question.explanation: The causal mask sets pre-softmax scores for future positions to −∞ so each token attends only to itself and earlier tokens.

slides.title: What to carry forward
slides.body: Self-attention = attention with Q,K,V from one sequence: $\mathcal{O}(1)$ path length (why it beats RNNs), $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ cost (the central scaling pain), and a mandatory causal mask for decoders. Next: **multi-head attention** — one weighting per query isn't enough.
